hero.title: Document Apostille for International Use
hero.subtitle: Get guidance to prepare and apostille your documents for use abroad.

about.title: What is the Hague Apostille?
about.description: The Hague Apostille is a certificate that authenticates the origin of certain public documents so that they can be used in another country that is a party to the Hague Convention.
about.additionalInfo: In immigration, study, marriage, document recognition, and other international proceedings, certain documents may need to be apostilled before being submitted to the authorities of the destination country.

important.title: Important
important.text: The apostille certifies the authenticity of the signature, seal, or stamp appearing on the document. It does not certidy the content of the document or replace a translation when one is required.

documents.title: Which documents may need an apostille?
documents.subtitle: The need to apostille a document depends on the country where it was issued, the country where it will be used, and the type of procedure.

items.title: Civil certificates
items.description: Birth, marriage, death certificates, and other civil registry documents.

items.title: Academic documents
items.description: Diplomas, certificates, academic transcripts, and other documents related to academic qualifications.

items.title: Notarial documents
items.description: Powers of attorney, declarations, and other documents formalized before a notary.

items.title: Judicial documents
items.description: Certain documents and certificates issued by judicial authorities.

items.title: Public certificates
items.description: Certificates and documents issued by public bodies or authorities.

items.title: Other documents
items.description: Depending on the procedure, other documents may also be subject to apostille requirements.
